contentStatusNote: Personal-use publication after source verification and automated checks; no independent human, clinical or NIA endorsement.

timeContext.explanation: The NIA older-adult guide recommends 30-minute strength sessions. This is its guideline time allocation, not a measured completion estimate for the repository’s six-exercise arrangement. Warm-up, instruction and untimed rest can make the session longer; do not rush to meet a time budget.

summary: An original three-day nonconsecutive arrangement using the NIA older-adult strength framework and verified movement versions. The source allows two or more strength days; this three-day calendar is an authored example, not evidence that three days are superior.

designedToSupport: Organizing three nonconsecutive source-scoped strength-practice sessions.
doesNotGuarantee: Specific strength, hypertrophy, injury-prevention or rehabilitation outcomes.
A benefit over the two-day template or suitability for every older adult.
notDesignedFor: Diagnosis, rehabilitation, athletic peaking or individualized medical clearance.

bestFor: Older adults seeking a simple source-based strength-practice framework after confirming suitability and learning each movement.
notFor: People with unresolved pain, illness, balance limitations or medical concerns requiring individualized advice.
A novice who has not learned the intermediate bench-supported row.
prerequisites: Able to use a stable wall, sturdy chair and bench safely.
Prior instruction and comfortable control of all listed movements; the ACE row is intermediate.
assumptions: The NIA older-adult guide is used for general educational context, not individualized prescription.
The original arrangement and exercise order have not been tested as a whole.

restDayGuidance: The NIA guide recommends strength exercise on two or more days, without training the same muscle group on consecutive days.
Monday, Wednesday and Friday are an original nonconsecutive scheduling example; three days are not claimed to outperform two.

trigger: Two sets of 10–15 repetitions become easy with the source-described control.
action: For the weighted exercises, increase the weight at the next session as described in NIA page 42; no fixed increment is prescribed here.
ceiling: Keep controlled movement; do not lift more than can be managed or force very, very hard effort.
floor: If eight repetitions cannot be managed, use a lighter weight; build gradually and start the first week light or unloaded.
stallResponse: Retain or reduce the weight and practise control; do not invent a loading increment or push through pain.

trigger: The stated wall push-up, unloaded squat or chair-supported two-leg toe stand can be performed with control.
action: Maintain the source-described version rather than automatically adding load or transferring a different variant’s prescription.
ceiling: Do not change to machine calf raises or elevated-bench push-ups under this program version.
floor: Begin with what can be managed; stop before loss of the source-described control. Seek instruction if this version is unsuitable.
stallResponse: Pause progression and obtain qualified instruction rather than forcing the target.

substitutionGroups.displayName: NIA seated or standing overhead press
matchingRules: The NIA page-47 overhead-press instruction permits sitting or standing; retain the same source framework.
Use the position already learned and appropriate to your balance and support needs.
disallowedChanges: Do not treat the standing position as automatically safer or more effective.
Do not substitute a barbell or machine press using these instructions.

scienceRationale.decision: Retain a fixed, nonconsecutive three-day calendar as an original example within the NIA two-or-more-days framework.
qualifiers: The linked consistency topic is practical education; it does not establish a superiority effect for this template.
Dose and day spacing come from the NIA older-adult guide; the complete arrangement is original repository work.
The frequency topic separates frequency from other training variables; this authored template is not a tested superiority comparison.

measurementGuidance.howToUse: Track completed sessions only if you choose local tracking; missing sessions are not automatically failures.
limitations: Completion does not prove adaptation, safety, readiness or suitability.

generalBoundaries: Use slow controlled movement, breathe continuously and retain the described support.
Consult a qualified professional when unsure about suitability, after surgery or with health concerns.
stopSignals: Stop for chest pain or pressure, severe joint pain, dizziness, feeling sick or other warning symptoms described by NIA.
professionalReviewTriggers: Pain, illness, recent surgery or difficulty using the source-described positions.
